Operators on bitmaps

Source: R/algebra.R
zuroar-ops.Rd

Between two bitmaps, | is the union and & the intersection, each a new bitmap. == and != test equality, x <= y whether x is a subset of y, x < y whether it is a strict subset, and >= and > the reverse; each returns a single TRUE or FALSE.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'zuroar'
Ops(e1, e2)

# S3 method for class 'zuroar64'
Ops(e1, e2)

Arguments

e1, e2

Bitmaps, or a bitmap and a single whole number.

Value

A bitmap, or a single logical for the comparisons.

Details

Between a bitmap and a single whole number k, x + k, k + x and x - k shift every value by k, as roar_shift() does. A value that would leave the domain from 0 to 2^32 - 1 is an error; use roar_shift(drop = TRUE) to drop such values instead.

Everything else is a zuroar_error_unsupported error, because a set has no sensible answer:

  • !x would need a universe; use roar_flip() over a range.

  • x - y between bitmaps: use roar_andnot(). x ^ y means power in R; use roar_xor().

  • x > 5 and other comparisons with numbers would expand the set into a logical vector; use x & roar_range(6, 4294967295) or roar_contains().

Examples

x <- roar(c(1, 5, 9))
y <- roar(c(5, 9, 12))
x | y
#> <zuroar> 4 values in [1, 12]: 1 5 9 12
x & y
#> <zuroar> 2 values in [5, 9]: 5 9
x <= y
#> [1] FALSE
roar(5) < y
#> [1] TRUE
x + 10
#> <zuroar> 3 values in [11, 19]: 11 15 19
